questions.question: When passing a truck on a two-lane road, when should you return to your original lane?

options.text: When you can see the front of the truck in your rearview mirror.
As soon as the truck is behind you.
When you feel you have enough space.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the front of the truck in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Wait to return to your lane until you can see the entire front of the truck in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: It connects the front and rear brakes together when you use the rear brake.
It automatically brakes based on your riding habits.
It applies the brake when you downshift gears.

questions.correctAnswerText: It connects the front and rear brakes together when you use the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Some motorcycles have integrated braking systems. When you apply the rear brake, both the front and rear brakes work together. Check your owner's manual for your motorcycle's specific braking system.

questions.question: When you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Do both actions at the same time.
Only brake.
Do one action, then the other.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: Brake and swerve separately. Do one action first, then the other. Never do both at the same time.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, what is the best thing to do?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull onto the shoulder and wait for the rain to stop.
Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Roads become slippery when rain starts, especially in the center of the lane. Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles. The left tire track is often the safest choice.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield
Slow-moving vehicle
Railroad crossing

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle
questions.explanation: This sign is put on the back of slow-moving vehicles that go slower than 25 mph, such as farm equipment, construction vehicles, or horse-drawn wagons.

questions.question: When entering a curve, how should you position your motorcycle?

options.text: On the left side of the lane.
In a position that lets you see and be seen best.
In the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a position that lets you see and be seen best.
questions.explanation: Change your position in the lane to see and be seen better. In a left curve, ride on the right side of your lane to spot oncoming traffic earlier. In a right curve, ride on the left center to see ahead safely without being too close to oncoming vehicles.

questions.question: What portion of motorcycle and car collisions are caused by drivers failing to yield to motorcyclists?

options.text: One-quarter
More than half
One-half

questions.correctAnswerText: More than half
questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle and car crashes happen because drivers do not yield the right-of-way to motorcyclists. Never assume that drivers will yield to you, even if they are supposed to.

questions.question: A helmet gives the most protection when it has all of these qualities, except:

options.text: Meets U.S. DOT standards.
Is loose-fitting.
Has no defects.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is loose-fitting.
questions.explanation: A good helmet must meet U.S. Department of Transportation standards, fit snugly all the way around, and have no damage like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: If you will carry a passenger on your motorcycle, you will probably need to:

options.text: Lower the tire pressure.
Make no tire pressure changes.
Raise the tire pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Raise the tire pressure.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. Add a few pounds of air pressure to your tires before riding with a passenger. Check your owner's manual for the correct pressure.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid danger, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the front brake while swerving.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
questions.explanation: Do these actions one at a time, not together. Never brake while swerving because it can cause your motorcycle to tip over.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks up while you are stopping on a straight road:

options.text: You can usually keep control of the motorcycle.
You will likely lose control of the motorcycle.
You must release the rear brake to regain control.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can usually keep control of the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on a straight road, you can keep it locked until you stop completely. A locked rear wheel on an upright motorcycle traveling straight usually allows you to maintain control.

questions.question: Unless otherwise posted, the speed limit in residential areas is:

options.text: 20 mph.
25 mph.
30 mph.
40 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: 30 mph.
questions.explanation: The maximum speed limit in residential and business areas is 30 mph. Follow any posted speed limit signs if they show a different limit.

questions.question: Making eye contact with another driver:

options.text: Means they see you.
Does not mean they will properly yield to you.
Guarantees they will properly yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean they will properly yield to you.
questions.explanation: Never assume eye contact means another driver will yield to you. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists and still fail to see them.

questions.question: A motorized scooter can:

options.text: Only be operated during the day.
Be operated without a driver license.
Be operated with any class of driver license.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be operated with any class of driver license.
questions.explanation: In California, a motorized scooter can be used by anyone who has any class of driver license.

questions.question: A primary cause of single-vehicle motorcycle crashes is:

options.text: Riding too fast for weather conditions.
Turning too wide in a curve or turn.
Running off the road while avoiding another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning too wide in a curve or turn.
questions.explanation: A primary cause of single-vehicle motorcycle crashes is turning too wide in a curve. Turning too wide can cause your motorcycle to leave the road or hit an object.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
Yield to other drivers.
A stop sign is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: In the center of a traffic lane, there is usually an oily strip. Motorcyclists should:

options.text: Avoid riding on the oil and grease.
Not worry about the oil and grease.
Find the lane with the least amount of oil and grease.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid riding on the oil and grease.
questions.explanation: Avoid riding on oil and grease buildup. The oily strip is usually no more than two feet wide, so you can usually ride to the left or right side of it and still stay in the center part of the lane.

questions.question: How do convex mirrors differ from regular mirrors?

options.text: They show a narrower view of the road.
They show a wider view of the road.
They show a clearer view of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They show a wider view of the road.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors are common on motorcycles. They show a wider view than flat mirrors. However, they can make vehicles behind you look farther away than they actually are.

questions.question: Service signs are:

options.text: Orange with black letters.
Blue with white letters.
Green with white letters.

questions.correctAnswerText: Blue with white letters.
questions.explanation: Service signs are blue with white letters. They show where you can find rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: The center portion of a lane has an oily strip. This strip:

options.text: Should always be avoided.
Usually gives enough traction, unless it is raining.
Should only be used if you are sharing the lane with another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually gives enough traction, unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: The oily strip in the center of the road usually provides enough traction for safe riding, unless it is wet from rain. The oily strip is usually no more than two feet wide, so you can ride on either side of it and still be in the center portion of the lane.

questions.question: Oil drippings and debris collect most often in ______ of a lane.

options.text: The left portion
The middle portion
The right portion

questions.correctAnswerText: The middle portion
questions.explanation: Oil and debris from vehicles collect in the center of a lane.

questions.question: When another car is passing you, should you move to the far side of your lane?

options.text: Yes, it is recommended because you will be farther from the other vehicle.
No, it is not recommended because it may cause the other driver to move back into your lane too soon.
It does not matter because it has no effect on safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, it is not recommended because it may cause the other driver to move back into your lane too soon.
questions.explanation: Do not move to the far side of your lane when being passed. This can signal the passing driver to return to your lane before it is safe.

questions.question: What is true about convex mirrors?

options.text: They show a narrow view of the road behind you.
They show a wide view of the road behind you.
They are illegal.

questions.correctAnswerText: They show a wide view of the road behind you.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view than flat mirrors. Objects appear farther away than they really are. Get used to your mirrors if your motorcycle has convex mirrors.

questions.question: To make a quick turn on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Lean the motorcycle quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean the motorcycle quickly.
questions.explanation: To turn quickly, lean your motorcycle in the direction you want to go. Sharper turns need more lean.

questions.question: To turn safely on a motorcycle, you should always:

options.text: Lean in the direction of the turn.
Slow down while turning.
Turn using only the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: Always lean in the direction you are turning. Slow down before you enter the turn.
